solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pine for one tender to court daughter

parts.note: tender meat is soft
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A lovesick suitor pines for a gentle courtship of someone's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb of longing, but 'Pine for one' is an example of a kind of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine is a conifer, and timber from conifers is classed as this kind of wood.

clue.text: Cushy job initially selling popular drug remedy

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of selling

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: An easy job flogging a fashionable medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post paying well for little or no work, an easy number.

clue.text: Manage funds differently for entertainments

indicators.note: arranged differently means these letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Handling money another way to pay for amusements.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means frivolous amusement or lively high jinks.

clue.text: One who sees over time one's clever humour

indicators.note: over means covering, so the witness spreads over the other pieces

parts.note: a witness is one who sees an event
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An observer gains, over time, a sharp sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever, amusing remarks show quick wit, the quality of being funny and sharp.

clue.text: High-brow musical work the Queen admires primarily

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a musical work
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of admires

explanation.surface: A sophisticated composition is a favourite of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged drama sung throughout is often seen as an elite, cultured form of musical theatre.

clue.text: Extend study on Soviet Politburo leaders

indicators.note: in an across clue, study placed on the leaders means it comes after them
the leaders of the words Soviet and Politburo are their opening letters

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, as at university

explanation.surface: An order to widen research into the men at the top of the Soviet Politburo.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something out over a wider area is to make it cover more ground.

clue.text: Rubbish lawyer, one with two black eyes?

parts.note: to pan something is to criticise it harshly, to rubbish it
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A useless lawyer who has been beaten up and has two shiners.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition suggests a brawler; it is the animal with black eye patches.
explanation.definitionFit: The bear has black patches round both eyes, a playful description of the animal.

clue.text: I shot subordinate of ensign at the front

indicators.note: in a down clue the subordinate comes below, so the shot goes beneath the letter
at the front points to the first letter of ensign

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a go

explanation.surface: A soldier confesses to having shot a junior officer under an ensign.
explanation.definitionFit: The self, the 'I' of psychology, is one's sense of personal identity.

clue.text: Fellow describing flipping yours truly as a fiend

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing around, so the fellow encloses the other piece

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the words for the speaker are read backwards

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A man portrays the speaker, annoyingly, as a devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse word; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an evil spirit or devil.

clue.text: Crafty GM in chess Short annoyed

indicators.note: annoyed suggests these letters are stirred up into a new order
short means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A wily grandmaster plays chess against Nigel Short, who is irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Short is an English chess grandmaster, but here 'Short' trims 'chess' to CHES before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting and devious behaviour is crafty, cunning conduct.

clue.text: Woman granny cannibalised (reportedly)

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: granny is NAN, and a granny who has been cannibalised was ate, in British speech pronounced 'et'

explanation.surface: A gruesome tale of a grandmother who was eaten by cannibals.
explanation.walkthrough: In much British speech 'ate' is said 'et', so 'Nan ate' sounds like the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a female given name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Follow the rules of conservative in fine fettle

parts.note: someone in fine fettle is on form, performing well

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who is doing well sticks to the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with accepted rules or standards.

clue.text: May one go out with enthralling Dutch runner

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the first pieces hold the abbreviation inside them

parts.note: may and can both express being permitted
one is the Roman numeral I
to go out with someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may go on a date with a captivating Dutch athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is not an athlete: it is someone who runs for office.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs in an election is a nominee standing for the post.

clue.text: Crime that makes clergyman lose head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A crime so shocking that a priest loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose head' suggests losing one's temper, but it means losing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Acts clear up after tumbling in this?

definitions.text: Acts clear up after tumbling in this?

indicators.note: tumbling means the letters fall about into a new order

explanation.surface: Performers clean up after acrobatics in a big show.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a lavish show where acts tidy up after tumbling routines.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand stage show or extravaganza with circus-style acts is called this as a noun.

clue.text: Cad with Irish accent's not British

indicators.note: not British means the abbreviation for British is taken out

parts.note: a brogue is a strong Irish (or Scottish) accent

explanation.surface: A scoundrel with an Irish lilt who is not a Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a dishonourable man, and so is a rascal or scoundrel.

clue.text: Lively article one friend finally read

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
one is the Roman numeral I
a mate is a friend

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word read

explanation.surface: An item that one pal ended up reading was full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Something animated is full of movement and spirit, so vivacious.

clue.text: Friendly catholic absorbed by self-doubting question?

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the following phrase

parts.note: a person unsure of themselves might ask, am I able?

explanation.surface: A sociable Catholic becomes wrapped up in questioning his own worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The self-doubting question 'Am I able?' runs together to give the letters AMIABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly, characterised by goodwill.

clue.text: When individual internalises one malicious remark

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: internalises means taking something inside, so the individual holds the numeral

parts.note: an individual is a person
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A person absorbs a single spiteful comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur or damaging attack on someone's reputation is this, as in casting it.

clue.text: Unbalanced? Indeed so, having to whirl about!

indicators.note: whirl about means spinning the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone agrees a thing is lopsided because it was spun around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsided or biased, favouring one party over the other.

clue.text: Breaking up can be wonderful

definitions.meaning: a British colloquial word for excellent, terrific

explanation.surface: A cheery thought that ending a relationship can be marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shattering and, informally in Britain, terrific.

clue.text: Possibly unhappy about wind-up

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: someone unhappy might be described as not up, i.e. down

explanation.surface: Someone may be glum about a practical joke played on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind-up is a tease or hoax, and so is a pretence put on to fool someone.

clue.text: Dance music record by Orbital originally

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of Orbital

explanation.surface: A club track released by the electronic band Orbital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genre of upbeat dance music from the 1970s.

clue.text: Dean's half-finished my interior design

indicators.note: half-finished means only the first half of the word Dean is kept

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: A dean's room makeover is only half complete.
explanation.definitionFit: The furnishing and decoration of a room is its decorative scheme.

clue.text: Old and wicked Greek character

parts.note: wicked and mega are both slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A villainous figure from ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' suggests evil, but here it is slang for great.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so a letter or character.

clue.text: Synopses of a bishop's religious treaties

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, followed by the S of the possessive
tracts are short religious treatises; treaties is a playful stand-in for treatises

explanation.surface: Summaries of a bishop's writings on faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary of a paper or article is a synopsis of its contents.

clue.text: Bit of a lather heading to any northern country

parts.note: a single sud is a bit of soapy lather

indicators.note: heading to means the first letter of the word any

explanation.surface: A little soap foam heads off toward some northern land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Might one create a ring of cattle?

definitions.text: Might one create a ring of cattle?

parts.words: Might one create a ring of cattle?
parts.note: a ring here is a sound, not a circle: the clanging item hung round a cow's neck

explanation.surface: Asks whether some object could gather cows into a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests a circle of cows; it is the sound made by the bell worn by one.
explanation.definitionFit: The bell hung on a cow rings as the animal moves, making a ringing noise.

clue.text: You might say Victoria Beckham is comic

definitions.meaning: a famous footballer's wife is an example of the wives and girlfriends of England players, known by an acronym

explanation.surface: A claim that a celebrity fashion designer is funny.
explanation.walkthrough: The acronym stands for Wives And Girlfriends of footballers; Victoria Beckham is married to David Beckham, the England footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is a wit, and the acronym describes famous footballers' partners.

clue.text: Trained doctor meeting unwell editor

parts.note: unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A qualified doctor visits an editor who is poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are drilled, that is trained through repeated exercises.

clue.text: Kid singer with wig on head

indicators.note: the wig sits on the head of the singer, so it comes first

parts.note: rug is slang for a toupee or wig
a rat is an informer, one who sings to the police

explanation.surface: A child vocalist performing in a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' looks musical, but in crime slang a singer is an informer, a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child is informally called a crawling little one, chiefly in American use.

clue.text: Captured renegade ran sneakily around cages

indicators.note: around means the caged letters are turned the other way
the words renegade ran sneakily hold the letters inside them as a cage holds a bird

explanation.surface: A traitor who slipped away is caught and locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cages' holds DERANSNE in 'renegaDE RAN SNEakily'; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in a trap or snare, and so taken prisoner.
